newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: S&P affirms Air NZ credit ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms Air NZ credit ratings.

text.p: Ratings agency Standard & Poors Corp said on Tuesday it had affirmed Air New Zealand Ltd's BBB long term and A-3 short term credit ratings after Air New Zealand agreed on Monday to buy TNT Ltd's 50 percent stake in Ansett Airlines for a total A$475 million.
It said Air New Zealand's ratings outlook remained stable.
"In affirming Air New Zealand's ratings, Standard & Poors expects that the company will maintain healthy free cash flow levels and a moderately leveraged balance sheet," S&P said.

It said Air New Zealand's lease adjusted gearing increases to about 40 percent from just under 35 percent before the transaction. "Air New Zealand and News (Corp Ltd ) will seek gradually to improve Ansett's risk profile by rebuilding the balance sheet, reducing costs, improving asset utilisation and upgrading the fleet," S&P said.
"However, Ansett's exposure to high debt leverage and intense market competition are key credit concerns," it said.
Air New Zealand's ratings outlook remained stable.

"Despite the inherent cyclicality of the airline industry and the accompanying yield volatility, the company's strong business position and conservative financial policies afford downside protection," S&P said.
"The Ansett transaction will allow Air New Zealand to build a substantial regional alliance as a countervailing balance to competition from Qantas Airways Ltd," it said.
S&P also said TNT remained on creditwatch positive, awaiting a better assessment of the deal and an improvement in TNT's earnings capacity.
Air New Zealand's A shares were up eight cents at NZ$3.22 at 2.30 pm NZ time (0230 GMT).
